messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: routing-policy-service error-rate spike > 20% for smart-routing. Affected zone: eu-west-1. Pager channels: #incidents, @oncall-sre.

maria: seeing a flood of 502s for requests routed to variant 'gptx-legacy-small'. this is odd, traffic should be on 'gptx-v2' can anyone confirm?

sandeep: confirmed. dashboards show sudden fanout to legacy variant + region fallback thrash between eu-west-1 and eu-central-1.

devon: oncall here, I'm looking. starting a quick blast radius check — which customers hit?

jules: customer-impact report: ~12 customers with degraded responses, 3 high-traffic apps saw >30% error budget burn in last 5m. CS is pinged.

maria: stack traces point to model negotiation failures on the router: "VariantNotFoundError" then fallback policy kicks in. But why choose legacy?

sandeep: pulled the recent config schema migration from the prod-config repo. there's a new schema that deprecated `default_route` in favor of `route_policy`. some older deployments still have `default_route` set. looks like the validator let it through and the runtime interprets the old key as explicit fallback to 'gptx-legacy-small'.

devon: ugh. can you paste the snippet?

sandeep: ```yaml
# prod-config/smart-routing/2026-03-14.yaml
route_policy:
  - match: "region == 'eu' and model_tag == ~'gptx.*'"
    preferred: gptx-v2
# legacy default left behind
default_route: gptx-legacy-small
```

maria: so migrations = partial overlap. validator didn't reject `default_route` because of backwards compat logic, but runtime fallback precedence changed in the new server runtime (now treats `default_route` as higher priority). explains the sudden switch.

devon: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable legacy default routing on control plane, 2) rollback to pre-schema-migration config, or 3) patch runtime to ignore deprecated keys. shortest path is to flip off the deprecated key.

jules: CS update for customers in the loop: we are investigating routing anomalies, triage in progress. No SLA breaches confirmed yet but we are tracking. customers affected: ACME, Nimbly, Docutech.

devon: executing immediate mitigation: `redwood config patch smart-routing --unset default_route --env prod` 

maria: heads-up: that command will cause a config diff and trigger a config reload. doing it now in canary region first (eu-central-1) then eu-west-1.

oncall-bot: Deploy started by devon. Change ID: ch-2026-3467. Canary: eu-central-1.

sandeep: metrics after canary: error-rate in eu-central-1 dropped from 22% -> 3% in 2m. p50 latency normalized.

devon: rolling to eu-west-1 now. executing same patch.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Change ch-2026-3467 completed for eu-west-1.

maria: routing normal across eu regions. fallback loops stopped. verifying long-tail errors.

jules: customer-success: ACME reporting degraded UX resolved. Nimbly confirms returns to normal. Docutech still seeing occasional timeouts (investigating a separate cache miss issue).

devon: summarize root cause for postmortem: config schema migration introduced a deprecated key (`default_route`) remaining in some service configs. runtime semantics changed so deprecated key was given precedence, causing unexpected fallback to legacy variant and region failover oscillation. validator didn't block due to backward-compat allowance.

maria: actions: 1) audit prod configs for leftover deprecated keys and remove or migrate. 2) update validator to warn+require explicit opt-in when deprecated keys present in prod. 3) add a runtime guard to log-and-ignore deprecated keys during canary-phase of new runtime. 4) send CS incident summary.

devon: creating incident ticket and assigning owners. ETA for full audit: 24h. I'll hand off to sandeep for remediation. I'm going to sleep-mode handoff in 30m.

oncall-bot: devon is handing off to sandeep for remediation. Next on-call: sandeep. Handoff TS: 3467892522.

sandeep: accepted handoff. starting a repo-wide grep: `git grep -n "default_route:\s" prod-config || true`. will open PRs to remove/deprecate entries.

jules: CS will prepare customer-facing timeline and provide any credits if required. will coordinate with legal if ACME escalates.

maria: logging notes for postmortem: observed ~18min of elevated errors, primary mitigation completed in ~6m after canary. total impact window 20m. no data exfiltration or model integrity issues.

devon: thanks team. please add any additional context to the ticket. I'll label this P1->resolved and add severity notes.

customer-success: leaving a note: ACME asked for root cause email, pls include the schema diff and steps taken.

sandeep: opened PR #1427 to migrate configs and PR #1428 to change validator rules. linking in the incident ticket.

maria: adding follow-ups: automated config lint job to run on PRs that touch routing configs, and an integration test that fails if deprecated keys are present in prod branches.

devon: handoff complete. tagging this thread resolved but keeping it open for the postmortem draft. :thumbsup:
